note: Questions the interview playbook asks, keyed by the gap codes `interview coverage` emits. Placeholders: {name}, {employer}, {title}, {skill}, {count}. Probes are follow-ups to pull for specifics (numbers, scope, outcomes). Domain probes are chosen from the role's title and industry; `general` always applies.

identity.name.question: What is your full name as you want it on a resume?

identity.email.question: Which email address should employers use?

identity.phone.question: Which phone number should go on the resume (or none)?

identity.location.question: Where are you based (city and region or country)? Are you open to relocation?

identity.links.question: Any links to include: LinkedIn, portfolio, GitHub, personal site, licence lookup?

identity.headline.question: In one line, how would you describe what you do professionally (for example "Senior software engineer, frontend platforms" or "ICU registered nurse")?

identity.work_authorization.question: Is there anything about work authorisation or visas that employers need to know? (Skip if not relevant.)

targets.roles.question: What roles or job titles are you aiming for next? Include adjacent titles you would consider.

targets.seniority.question: What level are you targeting: same level as now, a step up (lead, manager), or flexible?

targets.locations.question: Where do you want to work: remote, hybrid, on-site, which cities or countries?

targets.industries.question: Any industries you prefer or want to avoid?

summary.pitch.question: If a recruiter had ten seconds, what are the two or three things you most want them to know about you?
probes: What are you known for among colleagues?
Which of your results are you proudest of?

experience.none.question: Let's walk through your work history, most recent first. For your current or latest role: employer, your exact title, start month and year, end (or present), location, and whether it is full-time, contract or something else.

experience.next.question: What came before {title} at {employer}? Employer, exact title, start and end month and year, location, and employment type. Say "that's all" when we reach the beginning you want on a resume.

experience.scope.question: At {employer} as {title}: what was the scope? Team size, who you reported to, what you owned, budget or caseload or territory if any, and the main tools, systems or stack you used.
probes: How many people were on the team, and did anyone report to you?
What were you responsible for that nobody else was?

experience.stack.question: Which tools, technologies, systems, equipment or methods did you use day to day at {employer}? List as many as apply.

experience.achievements.few.question: Tell me about {count} more things you accomplished at {employer} as {title}. For each: what was the situation, what did you do, and what changed as a result? Numbers help: percentages, money, time saved, volume, people, quality or safety measures.
probes: What would have happened if you had not done it?
How did you or your manager measure success?
Who else was involved, and what was specifically your part?

experience.metrics.none.question: None of the achievements at {employer} have a number yet. Can you quantify any of them: how much faster, cheaper, bigger, more reliable, how many people or customers, what rating or score? Estimates are fine if you say they are estimates.

achievement.weak.question: "{text}" reads as a duty rather than a result. What was the outcome, and how big was it?
probes: What was the before and after?
Did anyone outside your team notice?

skills.few.question: Let's build your skills inventory. List the skills, tools, technologies, certifications-in-use, methods and soft skills you would want a hiring manager to see, roughly grouped (for example technical, tools, domain, leadership, languages).

skills.level.missing.question: For {skill}: how would you rate yourself (beginner, intermediate, advanced, expert), how many years have you used it, and when did you last use it?

skills.evidence.none.question: You listed {skill} as a skill, but no role or project mentions it. Where did you use it, and for what?

education.none.question: Education: institution, degree or program, field, start and end year, and honours or relevant coursework if you want them shown. If none applies, say so.

certifications.none.question: Any certifications, licences or registrations (with issuer, year and expiry if relevant)? If none, say so.

projects.none.question: Any projects worth showing that are not covered by a job: side projects, open source, research, a business, a community effort? If none, say so.

languages.none.question: Which languages do you speak, and at what level? If only one, say so.

volunteering.none.question: Any volunteering, board or community roles you would want on a resume? If none, say so.

awards.none.question: Any awards, recognition, promotions-as-recognition or publications and talks? If none, say so.

documents.none.question: Do you have an existing resume, CV, LinkedIn export or portfolio I can read first? Paste it or give me the path. I will extract candidate facts and confirm each one with you before saving anything.

general: Who benefited from this, and how would they describe the change?
What did it cost or save in time, money or effort?
engineering: What were the scale and performance numbers (users, requests, latency, uptime, data volume)?
What did you own end to end versus contribute to?
Which architecture or design decisions were yours?
How was quality measured (test coverage, incidents, lead time, deployment frequency)?
leadership: How many people did you lead, hire or mentor, and what happened to them?
Which decisions did you make without escalating?
How did the team's output or health change under you?
healthcare: What was the unit, patient population, acuity and nurse-to-patient ratio?
Which protocols, equipment or systems did you use (for example EHR, ventilators, infusion pumps)?
Any measurable outcomes: patient satisfaction scores, infection rates, falls, readmissions, audit results?
Did you precept, train or lead others?
sales: What was the quota and your attainment per year?
Average deal size, cycle length, territory or book of business?
Which accounts did you win or grow, and by how much?
operations: What volume did you handle (orders, shipments, units, tickets)?
Which process changes did you introduce, and what did they improve?
finance: What size of budget, portfolio or book did you own?
Which reports, models or closes were yours?
Any audit findings, savings or accuracy improvements?
education: How many students, what levels, what outcomes (scores, pass rates, growth)?
Which curricula or programs did you design?
trades: What types of jobs, sites or equipment did you work on?
Any safety record, certifications or inspections passed?
Did you supervise apprentices or crews?
creative: What audience size, engagement or revenue did the work reach?
